notes: Field elements are hex, big-endian here for readability; on the wire they are 32-byte little-endian. The scenario uses a test verifier that accepts exactly one 480-byte proof: "valid-proof" padded with zeros. eventsH is the byte string of SPEC-WIRE §6 whose SHA-256 enters the digest. rejected lists the envelopes an indexer must refuse; the reason is informative, only the refusal is normative.

sections.envelopes: Each envelope of the scenario and of the reorg: its bytes, and for a spend its bodyHash (SPEC-WIRE §4: SHA256("sh20/v0/body" ‖ body) mod r, body from "SH20" up to the proof). Only envelopes that decode are listed: the three with an OP_RETURN payScript are only in blocks 15 and 16.
sections.claim: One CLAIM: the message SHA256("sh20/v0/claim" ‖ listTxid ‖ npk) and its BIP340 signature by lockKey, with 32 zero bytes of auxiliary randomness.
sections.preActivation: digest_{A-1}: the digest an indexer starts from at block A.
sections.carriers: One transaction each, and what SPEC-WIRE §3 finds in it. expect is the hex of the one counted envelope, "none" when no envelope is counted (an envelope of another version alone is "none"), a list of hex when they are a batch (two or more TRANSFERs, all in the witness: each applies alone), or "many" when two or more are counted otherwise (the transaction is refused). Inputs give their witness only; their outpoints play no part. {"coinbase": true} is the input of a coinbase; its witness, when given, is not read.
sections.scenario.verifierCalls: Every call to the verifier, in order, with its nine public inputs in the order of SPEC-WIRE §4: R[anchorHeight], nf0, nf1, leaf0, leaf1, leaf2, bodyHash, vPub, tPub. The proof is checked last (§5), so a spend refused for another reason is not in the list. In a batch, envelope is the index of the envelope in the transaction (also in rejected). An anchor below A is checked against the empty root.
sections.scenario.after: For each block: root R[H], the event types, eventsH, and digest_H.
sections.scenario.blocks: The transactions of each block. vin[].prevHeight is the height of the block that confirmed the output an input spends, given where a DEPLOY needs it (SPEC-WIRE §5: its commit must be N = deployMaturity blocks old; here N = 3). The window is W = 12 here (anchorWindow), so blocks 12 and 14 reach its lower end.
sections.reorg: After the scenario, blocks 16 and 17 give way to the two blocks given here: roll back to rollbackTo, then apply them. 16' spends the nullifiers of the TRANSFER of the first 16 again, which only a rollback allows. after is what an indexer that never saw the first 16 and 17 computes.

claim.note: BIP340 signature with 32 zero bytes of auxiliary randomness, by the key whose secret is SHA256("lock2-secret")

preActivation.note: Blocks below A have no root and no digest. digest_{A-1} = SHA256("sh20-v0"), whatever an indexer read before A.
